title: Anomaly Sentinel: Hypotheses and Remediation Catalog for Onboarding Eval Spikes
content:
Executive summary:

This note synthesizes the anomaly signal burst we saw across multiple onboarding evals (week of 2025-10-26) and proposes a prioritized catalog of hypotheses + remediation experiments. This is intended to be operational: short-lived mitigation steps that reduce customer impact in the next 2–4 weeks, plus medium-term runtime/decoder changes for Q1.

Top-level observations (TL;DR):
- Multiple onboarding suites showed a sharp increase in hallucination and entity-swap errors starting 2025-10-27. The spike correlates with two changes: a tokenizer patch rolled 2025-10-26 and an updated instruction template used by the onboarding harness (v3).
- Error surface is multi-modal: length-bias (overly terse or truncated evidence), entity-swap (confusion between entity types), and structured-output collapse (enumeration/JSON outputs malformed).
- Quick mitigations (canaryable): prefix-stabilization (force canonical system prompt), revert tokenizer patch to prior minor version, enable conservative beam constraints. Medium-term: add prompt scaffolding tests to onboarding harness, add token-boundary regression tests to the compilation pipeline, and build a small reranker service for high-risk prompt archetypes.

Methodology and signal sources:
- Data: onboarding eval sets from three customers (A, B, C) + internal anchor suites.
- Signals: automated metric regression alerts (hallucination-score increase, entity-consistency drop), sample-based manual triage, token-level logs with prefix/KV cache traces, and per-model sharding telemetry (latency, batch size, kernel selection).
- Triaging steps: 1) isolate failing prompt archetypes using simple clustering on prompt templates; 2) reproduce failures with deterministic seeds in infra; 3) generate counterfactual prompts to test hypothesis (e.g., add explicit entity types, expand system instruction).

Anomaly clusters (observed patterns and representative examples):

1) "Length-bias drift" (high frequency)
- Symptom: model drops crucial context mid-answer or returns very short answers where baseline returned long, reasoned outputs.
- Trigger archetype: open-ended summarization prompts with long context + system instruction that encourages concision. Examples: "Summarize the following discussion into action items (no more than 2 sentences)" with 2.5k token contexts.
- Probable causes: tokenizer patch altered token counts for some unicode ranges -> shifting kernel decisions and KV cache sizes; runtime batching heuristics caused early cache trimming; updated instruction template introduced explicit brevity signal.
- Quick mitigations: incrementally relax system prompt brevity constraint in canary (10% onboarding traffic), temporarily force larger max_length and disable early KV eviction for canary models.
- Medium-term: add tokenized-length delta test in model onboarding (compare token counts pre/post tokenizer changes) and update autoscaler heuristics to consider sequence-length distributions.

2) "Entity-swap hallucinations" (medium frequency, high severity for some tenants)
- Symptom: factual entity fields are swapped (e.g., company names, dates), sometimes mixing entities across context paragraphs.
- Trigger archetype: multi-entity extraction or transformation prompts ("extract: Name, Company, Date") and prompts that reuse identical placeholder tokens across examples.
- Probable causes: attention aliasing at long context lengths combined with subtle tokenization boundary differences that change alignment of separators/comma tokens; KV cache re-use across batched requests with shared prompt scaffolding (insufficient cache isolation).
- Quick mitigations: enable per-request KV namespace isolation for canary; add simple heuristic reranker to check extracted entities against direct substring matches in source and demote outputs with low overlap.
- Medium-term: instrument attention head attributions in failing cases; add a lightweight static analyzer in the harness that flags examples where token boundaries for entity mentions shifted between tokenizer versions.

3) "Structured-output collapse" (low frequency, reproducible)
- Symptom: enumerations/JSON outputs lose separators or close braces, returning malformed JSON.
- Trigger archetype: prompts that request strict JSON or list outputs (often used by customers to parse automated responses).
- Probable causes: decoder sampling temperature changes due to new kernel scheduling; or post-processing strip logic applied incorrectly when trailing whitespace tokens are different under new tokenizer.
- Quick mitigations: for routes flagged as structured-output, switch to constrained decoding / deterministic beam for canary traffic; also run a post-formatter that attempts minimal repairs (close braces, comma fixes) before returning to customers.
- Medium-term: add unit tests in onboarding harness that validate structural outputs and fail builds if a new tokenizer variant changes trailing-token distributions for common delimiter characters.

Cross-cutting root causes and confidence levels:
- Tokenizer patch (rolled 2025-10-26) — high confidence as multiple failing examples show token offsets vs archived baseline.
- Onboarding harness instruction template v3 — medium confidence; several suites use it and it introduces stronger brevity signals.
- Runtime KV re-use optimization change — low-to-medium confidence; reproductions suggest cache isolation changes can be correlated to entity leakage in batched scenarios.

Experiment plan (short horizon, canaryable):
- Experiment E1: Revert tokenizer patch on canary cluster (10% traffic) and measure hallucination-score and entity-consistency for 72 hours. Metric definitions: entity-consistency = fraction of extracted entities matching exact source substrings; hallucination-score = fraction of outputs with OOV facts as judged by string-match and sample human review. Owner: Diego. Linked ticket: JIRA-ML-4823.
- Experiment E2: Apply prefix-stabilization (canonical system prompt) to onboarding harness + lock max_length to baseline for 7 days. Canary at 5%. Owner: Samira. Success criteria: hallucination-score improvement >= 20% and no latency regression >5%.
- Experiment E3: Enable per-request KV namespace isolation for batched requests in runtime on a single GPU pool, run stress tests with multi-tenant simulated traffic. Owner: Linnea. Success criteria: elimination of cross-request entity leakage in synthetic harness.

Operational telemetry and dashboard queries to add:
- A view that tracks tokenized-length delta (new-token-count - archived-token-count) per prompt template; alert if mean delta > 2 tokens for > 5% of examples.
- Entity-overlap metric per onboarding suite (substring match rate).
- Structured-output parse-failure rate (JSON.parse errors per 1000 responses) filtered by route and model version.
- A sample-queue that auto-enqueues representative failing examples into the applied-ml triage board (linked to JIRA ticket).

Open questions / notes to self:
- Are any customers using third-party pre-tokenization or normalization before sending prompts? If so, we need to include them in the tokenization delta checks.
- Should we add a lightweight deterministic decoder mode to the hosted API specifically for structured-output routes? Pros/cons checklist needed.
- We should audit the rollout timeline of instruction template v3 (who pushed, which suites opted in) — this may reveal correlated changes that aren’t in our deployment logs.

Action items (owner, ETA):
- Diego: roll canary revert of tokenizer patch (E1) and report initial 72h metrics — ETA 2025-11-05.
- Samira: implement prefix-stabilization experiment (E2) and add canary config — ETA 2025-11-06.
- Linnea: run runtime isolation stress test (E3) and attach reproducer harness to JIRA ticket — ETA 2025-11-09.
- Riley (author): add tokenized-length delta check to onboarding CI and a small checklist for product onboarding to ensure structured-output routes are flagged — ETA 2025-11-15.

Appendix: short reproduction notes and example cases (copy-paste friendly)
- Case A (length-bias): prompt file: examples/case_A_long_summary.txt. Seeded command: python harness/run_eval.py --suite cases/A --model canary_tokenizer_revert --seed 42
- Case B (entity-swap): prompt snippet: "Extract: Name, Company, Role from the following text:" followed by multi-paragraph context. Repro steps logged in github.com/redwood-inference/evals/issues/129

If you want raw logs / sample outputs I collected in triage, ping me (Riley) and I’ll attach the per-request traces and KV cache dump for the failing runs. This doc is deliberately operational and noisy — prioritize experiments E1/E2 first, then E3.

-- end --
